description: The drawer keeps commit hashes behind a compact copy icon. The test harness has already stubbed the server's conversation list and cut off its live update stream, so there is nothing to set up, intercept or check about that (do not look at the API): the drawer (".drawer") shows the conversations the test names, as rows [data-conversation-id="<id>"] whose title (".conversation-title") is their slug, which is their id (drafts have none), and whose preview is "Preview". The list is "with-commit" (commit 424904d, subject "Make git graph file paths readable"), "hash-only" (commit abcdef1, no subject) and "no-commit". "The copy button" is the with-commit row's button "Copy commit hash 424904d". The clipboard may be read with eval "navigator.clipboard.readText()". Perform the numbered steps in order, each fully. A button "X" is the element with role button (a <button>) whose accessible name (aria-label, else its text) is exactly X; "There is no S", "no S" or "none" means no element matches at all: assert_count 0, never a visibility check. Whether an element "has the class X" is an eval of its classList.contains('X') (polled with expect), never a visibility check: a collapsed drawer may have no size. Every selector you need is given here, so do not explore the source code or read other tests (the old Playwright spec is being replaced and does not apply): write all the steps in one run_steps call right away, and look something up only if a step fails. A button "X" is button[aria-label="X"] when one exists (as for "Open conversations", "Search conversations...", "Search tasks...", "View options", "Show chapters", "Archive", "Restore" and "Delete"); otherwise it is the button whose visible text is exactly X, picked with has_text X (a substring match, so make sure no other button's text contains X), as for "Ask Shelley", "View Archived" and "Back to conversations". 1. Navigate to /new. 2. The copy button is visible. 3. The with-commit row's ".drawer-git-info" text is exactly "Make git graph file paths readable". 4. The copy button contains exactly 3 "circle" elements, and its "path" element's d attribute is exactly "M6 16.6V7.4M6 16.6C8 11 12 6 14.6 5". 5. Record the copy button's getBoundingClientRect() (x, y, width, height) in window.__copyBox; its width is at most 24. 6. Record its computed color in window.__restingColor. 7. Hover the copy button. 8. The element with role "tooltip" should contain the text "Click to copy 424904d". 9. The copy button's computed color should come to differ from window.__restingColor (poll: the hover color can land after the tooltip). 10. Click the copy button. 11. The clipboard should come to hold exactly "424904d". 12. The copy button has the class "drawer-git-copy-copied", contains no "circle" elements, and is focused (document.activeElement). 13. Its bounding rect's x, y, width and height are exactly those in window.__copyBox. 14. The URL's path is still exactly /new (eval "location.pathname"). 15. Focus the hash-only row's button "Copy commit hash abcdef1" (it is visible; eval its focus()) and press Enter. 16. The clipboard should come to hold exactly "abcdef1". 17. The URL's path is still exactly /new (eval "location.pathname"). 18. The no-commit row has no ".drawer-git-info".
